The premise is reversed. The document does not report that the 50%[1] Mn sample delivered more capacity. It reports the opposite: the 10%[2] Mn sample had the higher charge capacity, 212 mAh g^− 1 (10% Mn)[3] versus 164 mAh g^− 1[4] for the 50%[5] Mn sample. The document attributes this to the electrochemical inactivity of the Mn ions.

For heat, the 50%[6] Mn sample released less, not more. In the thermal decomposition tests the 10%[7] Mn sample gave 901.4 J g^−1 for 10% Mn[8], and the 50%[9] Mn sample gave 485.7 J g^−1 for 50% Mn[10]. The 50%[11] Mn sample therefore released about this many J/g less heat than the 10%[12] Mn sample: 415.7[13] J/g.
